title: PackBuildRequest
description: A durable record that a capability is MISSING. Creating one calls no model and writes no candidate file - it is a question, not a build. An authorized human starts the build; a mission never does, because an agent that can conjure its own tools inside a customer run has escaped every review the system has.

requested_by.description: The named person inside the tenant who asked. Tenant scope answers 'which company'; this answers 'who', which is what an audit row needs.

mission_id.description: The mission that discovered the gap, when there was one. Recorded for audit; it grants nothing.

capability_outline.description: Plain language, operator-supplied. Bounded because an unbounded field is a prompt-injection surface and a place customer text could accumulate.

domain.description: Metadata only. Domain selects knowledge and fixtures; it must never cause a branch in the kernel.

state.description: Named for who the request is waiting on, which is the only thing a queue reader needs. AWAITING_OPERATOR_START and AWAITING_BUILDER replaced REQUESTED and BUILD_STARTED: the old names described an intention, and BUILD_STARTED in particular lied by default - while no Builder exists, a request in that state has had nothing built. AWAITING_BUILDER says the true thing (an operator authorised it; it is queued) and keeps saying the true thing after the Builder lands. No PROMOTED state exists here, deliberately: promotion is a separate decision recorded in the pack registry by a human, never a transition this record can make.

expected_accepts.description: Contract NAMES, not prose. An intent field that accepted free text would be where a prompt eventually lives; an identifier-shaped field cannot carry one.

handoff_intent.description: What the handoff is FOR, in bounded plain language.

prohibited_actions.description: What this Pack must never do, recorded at REQUEST time - before any model has an opinion - so the boundary is the requester's rather than the builder's.

requested_capability_reviews.description: Questions, not grants. Carried from request to proposal to reviewer unchanged; nothing here can trigger a tool call, alter a capability lease, or reach the runtime.

started_by.description: Null until a human starts the build. Its absence is what makes auto-start impossible to represent.

model_role.description: A ROLE, never a model name, endpoint or deployment.

model_identity.description: The configured identity actually used, recorded for audit after the fact. Never supplied by a Pack.
